references.text: The continuation of the text specifying which flying creeping things are permitted to eat: locusts, solam, hargol and hagab.
Parallel text about unclean flying creeping things that must not be eaten, part of the Mosaic purity laws.
The preceding verse declaring that flying creeping things that go on four legs are generally an abomination, from which verse 21 provides an exception.
Locusts are mentioned as one of the ten plagues in Egypt, showing that the Israelites were familiar with these insects.
John the Baptist ate locusts and wild honey, which was permitted food according to Mosaic law.
Mark confirms that John the Baptist ate locusts, which was in accordance with Mosaic dietary rules.
